hints: Find the driving force from power and speed: $F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{960000}{30} = 32000\text{ N}$.
At constant speed up the incline, driving force balances resistance plus the component of weight down the slope: $F_D - mg\sin\alpha - R = 0$.
Substitute $mg\sin\alpha = 75000(10)(0.01) = 7500\text{ N}$ and solve for the resistance $R$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force of the engine at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with power $960\text{ kW} = 960000\text{ W}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{960000}{30} = 32000\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces along the slope for motion at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - mg\sin\alpha - R = 0$$
$$32000 - 75000(10)(0.01) - R = 0$$
$$32000 - 7500 - R = 0$$
$$R = 24500\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Finds $F_D = 32000\text{ N}$ and solves $32000 - 7500 - R = 0$ to get $R = 24500\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship connecting power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D v$$
Substitute $P = 960\text{ kW} = 960000\text{ W}$ and $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$960000 = F_D (30)$$
$$F_D = \frac{960000}{30} = 32000\text{ N}$$

Identify the forces acting on the railway engine parallel to the incline:
- Forward driving force: $F_D = 32000\text{ N}$
- Downward component of weight: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha$
- Resistance force opposing motion: $R$

Calculate the component of weight down the slope using $m = 75000\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\alpha = 0.01$:
$$W_{\parallel} = (75000)(10)(0.01) = 7500\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law for constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$\sum F = 0$$
$$F_D - W_{\parallel} - R = 0$$
$$32000 - 7500 - R = 0$$
$$24500 - R = 0 \implies R = 24500\text{ N}$$
Thus the constant resistance force is $24\,500\text{ N}$.

hints: Calculate the work done by the engine in $60\text{ s}$: $W_{\text{engine}} = P \times t = 900000 \times 60 = 54000000\text{ J}$.
Calculate the work done against the constant resistance $24500\text{ N}$ over $1900\text{ m}$: $W_{\text{res}} = 24500 \times 1900 = 46550000\text{ J}$.
Apply the work-energy principle on horizontal track: $\Delta E_k = W_{\text{engine}} - W_{\text{res}}$, add to initial kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}(75000)(30^2)$, and solve for the final speed $v$.
walkthrough:
Calculate work done by the engine and work done against resistance over the $1900\text{ m}$ horizontal section:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = 900000 \times 60 = 54000000\text{ J}$$
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = 24500 \times 1900 = 46550000\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy principle to find the change in kinetic energy:
$$\Delta E_k = W_{\text{engine}} - W_{\text{resistance}} = 54000000 - 46550000 = 7450000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the initial kinetic energy and total final kinetic energy:
$$E_{k,\text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}(75000)(30^2) = 33750000\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k,\text{final}} = 33750000 + 7450000 = 41200000\text{ J}$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work\u2013Energy Principle: Calculates $W_{\text{engine}} = 54\text{ MJ}$, $W_{\text{res}} = 46.55\text{ MJ}$, sets up work-energy equation, and gets $v = 33.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $10\sqrt{11}\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy theorem for horizontal motion: because the track is horizontal, there is no change in gravitational potential energy ($\Delta E_p = 0$). The net work done on the engine equals its change in kinetic energy:
$$\Delta E_k = W_{\text{engine}} - W_{\text{resistance}}$$

Calculate the work done by the engine operating at a constant rate of $900\text{ kW} = 900000\text{ W}$ for $t = 60\text{ s}$:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = P \times t = (900000\text{ W})(60\text{ s}) = 54000000\text{ J} = 54\text{ MJ}$$

Calculate the work done against the constant resistance force $R = 24500\text{ N}$ over distance $s = 1900\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = R \times s = (24500)(1900) = 46550000\text{ J} = 46.55\text{ MJ}$$

Calculate the net gain in kinetic energy:
$$\Delta E_k = 54000000 - 46550000 = 7450000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the initial kinetic energy at speed $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,\text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}mu^2 = \frac{1}{2}(75000)(30^2) = (37500)(900) = 33750000\text{ J}$$

Add the kinetic energy gain to find the final kinetic energy:
$$E_{k,\text{final}} = E_{k,\text{initial}} + \Delta E_k = 33750000 + 7450000 = 41200000\text{ J}$$

Solve for the final speed $v$:
$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 41200000$$
$$37500 v^2 = 41200000$$
$$v^2 = \frac{41200000}{37500} = \frac{3296}{3} = 1098.667$$
Take the square root:
$$v = \sqrt{\frac{3296}{3}} = 10\sqrt{11} \approx 33.166\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$v = 33.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus the speed of the engine at the end of the $60\text{ s}$ is $33.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $10\sqrt{11}\text{ m s}^{-1}$).
